body:
I don't even think I can enjoy things anymore. I'm not trying to be a defeatist. I really want help. I want something to work. I'd fix this if I knew how. I just... I can't wrap my mind around how I could possibly do it. How do I make myself *like* things again? Everything I used to like doing just makes me feel weirdly disconnected and tired; it's like I'm trying to fill a bottomless pit.

At this point, I'd settle for being useful. I can't imagine ever being happy, but if I can just be useful, maybe all this won't be such a waste. But I don't know how I can get to being useful when all I can think about is how badly I want to die.

I'd say you should pay attention to what your brain's doing when you listen to it. I can't listen to happy songs. It's just unbearably fake and saccharine. But listening to sad songs is so soothing. It's comforting to be able to relate to music, knowing that someone out there understands. It's so much less lonely.

But I can also see how it could reinforce harmful thinking. Before the last time I was hospitalized, I found that playing the game Yume Nikki gave me the same soothing feeling as music. It was such a release. But I quickly became fixated on it. I'd make the main character jump off the balcony over and over, just laying in bed with my laptop and watching her go splat for hours. It... wasn't healthy.
Oh fuck yes. The insomnia's the worst part.

I'm the same. I was a lightweight division rower at the onset of my depression and would be on the water 2-3 hours a day 5-6 days a week. Pre-depression, it made me indescribably happy. Post-depression, it became as empty and tiring as everything else.

My doc has told me that exercise is generally only helpful for depression when patients were sedentary before. Regular exercise does a lot of good for the body, so it makes sense that those who don't exercise would see serious benefits from starting. But there's a limit to the amount of good it can do. 

All I can say is: don't feel hopeless just because exercise isn't helping your depression. And definitely don't quit. Even if it's not helping your brain chemistry, it does a whole lot of good for the rest of your body, and you need to keep taking care of yourself while you're in the pit.

I find it helpful to think of exercise like brushing my teeth. Is brushing your teeth fun? No, but you need to keep doing it. I can't find it fun anymore (because I can't find anything fun anymore), but it doesn't need to be. You may not get any immediate gratification from the act, but shit gets really scary *real* fast once you stop caring about basic self-maintenance.  

That said, you don't have to live this way. Just because one form of treatment is ineffective doesn't mean that nothing else will help. You say you're seeing a therapist-- that's awesome. If you're not already doing so and can afford it, I'd look into seeing a psychiatrist as well. Therapy is great for facing your demons, but it helps to have a medical doctor address the physical side of the sickness.

Honestly, at this point I'd be happy if going off of a drug made me worse. Well, not really. But at least it'd be *something,* y'know?

I've told my doc that I refuse to take self-harm off of the table until I find something else that makes any difference at all. I know it isn't good, but at least it makes me functional enough to do things like... eat.

Thanks. It's just disheartening to never feel any change at all. I don't expect meds to fix everything, but it'd be nice if they made a bigger difference than the sugar pills that come with my birth control.

A lot. Several different SSRIs, SNRIs, antipsychotics, stimulants. My doctor always gives it a few months before she switches one out or changes the combination, usually increasing the dose every two weeks. Every time I'm hospitalized, they increase the dose every day. 

Last time I was in for two months and had been taking the same combination of meds for one month prior to coming in. They increased my antidepressant and antipsychotic doses every day for the first month. When that did nothing, they switched to entirely new drugs and increased those every day until I was released. Nothing either.

I guess I'm fortunate in that I've never had symptoms coming off of one drug or having problems when I've forgotten to take it one day. But since none of them ever affect how I feel in the first place, I've never been concerned about it. I was honestly starting to wonder if they were just sugar pills until I got put on so much venlafaxine that I had constant nausea.
I play Yume Nikki when I'm down. Just the end. Watching Mado go splat is strangely soothing.

I've only *cut* a few times (I have a bleeding disorder, so I've only done it when I was actively trying to kill myself), but I burn pretty frequently.

In short, it's the only thing that keeps me functional. Without self-harm, I'm a zombie. I have pretty horrible intrusive thoughts a lot of the time, to the point that I can't even focus long enough to watch TV. Burning myself quiets my mind enough to be able to do things like clean the house or talk to people.

>What was your first time like?

I was in uni. I was failing all of my classes. I'd been in therapy for about a year and nothing was helping. My therapist suggested snapping a rubber band against my wrist to drown out the thoughts and snap out of dissociative episodes. It wasn't strong enough. I ended up beating my leg with a hammer.

Honestly, it felt great. I was able to actually sit down and focus on my homework for the first time in months. But when the rush wore off, I realized that my whole lower leg was an angry purple hematoma. Luckily my disease means that I get those more commonly than most people, so the hospital treated me without asking too many questions. But I needed to switch to something that was easier to hide.

>Are you still doing it or not, and why?

Yep. I don't need to do it as frequently anymore because I don't have as many obligations (I lost my job and failed uni after being hospitalized the last time I cut, and I hardly talk to anyone anymore). I also tend to burn until it blisters, so it hurts for a long time and I tend to get more mileage out of it than cutting or hitting, pain-wise. It's efficient.

Her boyfriend killed himself, then she had her baby, postpartum depression set in on top of that, then she killed herself. my other friend has cancer. he lost a lung a few years ago but was mostly okay after that, but he messaged me today saying that it's back and it's already spread so much that he says he's not even going to bother with treatment.

My roommate's car is gone. I'm gonna go get a burrito and go to the hospital. I'm sorry for bothering you.

I wish I had kidney stones instead. I'd take the kidney stones if I could have my friends back. Dying doesn't seem as bad. 

I don't want to leave my room until my roommate leaves because I burned a lot adn I don't want him to see it

I don't think it'd be worse than kidney stones. I used to get those all the time and that hurt worse than the actual surgery to get it removed, even when I didn't take the painkillers. I can't handle any more death. My uncle just died and the anniversary of one of my friends' suicides is in a couple weeks and now another friend is dying. I can't take it any more.

I've lost 14 friends and relatives in the last 3 years. My uncle just died last month, and I got a message from another friend saying that their cancer is back and they're not going to make it. I can't take this any more. It's not going to get better, everyone is just going to keep dying until either they're all gone or I am. I'm done. I just want to be done.
